definition: One sent by Jesus with his authority. The term refers chiefly to the Twelve and to Paul, whose teaching is the foundation of the church.
What God does through the death of Jesus to deal with sin and reconcile sinners to himself.
The collection of books recognized as Scripture. The Protestant Bible has 66 books, 39 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New.
A title meaning “anointed one,” the Greek form of “Messiah.” It names Jesus as the promised king and savior.
The people God has gathered to himself through Christ. The word describes both the whole body of believers and a local gathering of them.

A binding relationship God establishes with his people, with promises and obligations. The Bible tells its story through covenants with Noah, Abraham, Israel at Sinai, David, and the new covenant in Christ.
God bringing everything into being from nothing by his word, and the world he made and sustains.
God’s choice of a people for himself according to his own purpose and grace.
The study of last things: Christ’s return, the resurrection, judgment, and the new creation.
The removal of Israel and Judah from the promised land to Assyria and Babylon, a result of covenant unfaithfulness. It also describes humanity’s separation from God.
God’s rescue of Israel from slavery in Egypt. It becomes the pattern for later salvation in the Bible.
Trust in God and his promises, resting on what he has said and done, above all in Christ.
Adam and Eve’s disobedience in Eden, through which sin and death entered the world.
The good news that Jesus lived, died for sinners, rose again, and reigns, and that all who trust him are forgiven and made new.
God’s undeserved kindness toward sinners.
God’s moral perfection and his separateness from all that is common or sinful. His people are called to be holy as well.
The Son of God taking on a full human nature in Jesus, while remaining fully God.
The conviction that Scripture is God-breathed. God spoke through human authors so that their writings are his word (2 Timothy 3:16).
God declaring sinners righteous in his sight because of Christ, received by faith alone.
God’s rule and reign, present in Jesus and one day to be complete when he returns.
God’s instruction to Israel, especially in the first five books. It can also refer to the whole of the Old Testament.
The promised anointed king from David’s line. Christians confess that Jesus is that king.
A way of reading the Bible that sees God’s covenants unfolding step by step, each building on the last, and all reaching their fulfillment in Christ and the new covenant.
God’s word spoken through a prophet. It includes calls to repentance and promises of what is to come, not only prediction.
A sacrifice that turns away God’s wrath. In the New Testament it describes Christ’s death in the place of sinners.
God’s continuing care for and rule over all things, working all events toward his purposes.
Rescue by payment. The Bible uses it for God freeing his people from slavery and from sin.
Turning from sin to God, with a change of mind, heart, and life.
Being raised bodily from death. Christ was raised first, and believers will follow when he returns.
A day of rest set apart to God, rooted in creation. It points to the rest God gives his people in Christ.
An offering given to God. The Old Testament sacrifices pointed ahead to the once-for-all sacrifice of Christ.
God’s rescue of his people from sin, death, and judgment, and the new life he gives.
The lifelong work of the Holy Spirit making believers more like Christ.
Rebellion against God, whether in what we do, fail to do, or desire.
The belief that there is one God who eternally exists as three persons, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
The way persons, events, and institutions in the Old Testament foreshadow Christ and his work.
In the Bible, skill in living under God’s rule, beginning with the fear of the Lord.
Honoring God for who he is, in praise, prayer, obedience, and all of life.
